title: Branching, Switching & The HEAD Pointer
description: Understand lightweight branches as movable pointers, inspect the HEAD reference, and switch contexts with git switch.

blocks.content: You want to try a new checkout screen while the current version stays safe. You need a separate line of work. What is the smallest Git action that keeps the work safe?

A branch is a movable label for a line of commits. `git switch -c feature-name` creates and enters a new branch without changing the main branch.

```mermaid
flowchart LR
    A["Working files"] -->|"choose an action"| B["Git history"] -->|"share or recover"| C["Team project"]
```

blocks.question: Why create a branch?
options: To try work without changing the main line
blocks.explanation: A branch gives experimental work its own line of commits.

blocks.prompt: Model the Git idea in a tiny simulator. Export a function named `branchFile` that takes `(working, staged, file)` and returns a new staged list containing `file` once. Do not change either input list.

tests.description: works when no working files are listed yet
